costliest.narrative: Training thunderstorms brought a swath of heavy rain to portions of southern Nebraska, beginning in Dawson County, and expanding into portions of northeast and east-central Nebraska. Areas upstream the Platte River, primarily in Merrick, Howard and Nance counties saw over 5 inches of rain with these storms. costliest.narrative: A fire started along Betty Way Road north of North Platte at approximately 1030 AM CT on February 26th. Aided by 40+ MPH westerly winds, the fire raced 26 miles east into western portions of Custer County. The fire was in very hilly, canyon type terrain, and was fueled by stands of cedar trees. This made attacking the fire difficult. By the 20th, improving weather conditions, allowed the fire to be contained. The main damage was to fencing as no structures were reported damaged.

Five homesteads were evacuated along State Farm Road between Newberry Access and Shack Road. A total of 13 fire departments aided in the fire and aerial support was brought in to aid in fire suppression. Evacuation orders were lifted by mid afternoon and the fire was contained around 6 PM CDT.  No structures were damaged in the fire and the fire was confined to pasture and canyon ground.

costliest.narrative: Fire initiated along highway 2 in the vicinity of the Cooksley Ranch, 6 miles northwest of Anselmo during the morning hours of April 12th. Known as the Cooksley Complex Fire, strong southerly winds pushed the fire to the north and north northwest during the afternoon hours of the 12th. Dry lightning and a wind shift forced the fire east on the 13th. By the time the fire was contained on the morning of April 14th, it had consumed approximately 37000 acres of rangeland. A home was destroyed at the McGinn Ranch and a bunkhouse was lost as well. Several calves were also lost in the fire in addition to outbuildings.

Fire broke out during the mid afternoon hours of February 24th. Aided by strong winds and low relative humidity, the fire consumed approximately 900 acres before being contained on February 26th. The fire then flared up and was renamed the East Table Fire. Two firefighters were injured on February 24th when their fire truck overturned in hilly terrain. The East Table Fire consumed an additional 450 acres before it was contained on March 3rd.  A third fire was reported over western portions of Custer County. Named the Eureka Valley Fire, this fire consumed approximately 4800 acres and burned from February 24th through March 3rd when it was finally 100 percent contained.

costliest.narrative: A fire initiated along a trail during the mid afternoon hours of October 2nd in north central portions of the Nebraska National Forest at Halsey. Aided by very strong southerly winds, the fire quickly spread to the north and north northwest consuming the Nebraska 4 H camp. At this camp, 18 buildings were destroyed including the main lodge. The fire then jumped the Middle Loup River and Nebraska highway 2 racing across several miles of open rangeland. One firefighter perished from a medical emergency while battling the fire. Approximately 200-250 different personnel battled this fire from the 2nd through the 11th. When the fire was fully extinguished, 19000 total acres had burned.

This Tuesday had an upper level trough axis making its way through central Canada and the Northern Plains, which pushed a strong surface cold front southeast across the local area during the day. Conditions were quiet through midday, with scattered storms starting to develop along this cold front during the early afternoon hours.  By 3 PM CDT, storms had erupted along the entire frontal boundary, which at that time was roughly along a line from Silver Creek, NE to Palco, KS. The main line of activity along surface front continued to push east through the day, but there were a few storms which lagged further west closer to the 850mb front. Though lower and mid-level lapse rates were less than ideal, mixed-layer CAPE mainly around 2000-2500 j/kg and sufficient deeper layer shear allowed for scattered storms to become strong to severe.
